diagnostic_evidence.quote: We aim to find the coefficients $ \bm{c} =(c_{\bm{\nu}_1},...,c_{\bm{\nu}_s})\in\C^s$, so we consider the linear system $ \bm{\Psi}  \bm{c} = \bm{b} $, with $ \bm{\Psi} \in\C^{m\times s}$ and $ \bm{b} \in\C^m$

issues.failure_explanation: The optimization variable is restricted to $\mathbb R^s$, while the target coefficients, design matrix, data, and displayed pseudoinverse solution are complex. For genuinely complex data the pseudoinverse solution need not be feasible, so the stated least-squares construction and results referring to it do not describe the claimed complex approximation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the feasible set $\mathbb R^s$ by $\mathbb C^s$ throughout the least-squares formulation and retain the Hermitian-adjoint normal equations.
issues.overall_effect: The complex-valued least-squares estimator used in the two convergence statements is not defined by the displayed program.
issues.title: Least-squares program excludes the complex coefficient vectors it is meant to recover
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the estimator's feasible field and does not change the method, rate, sample complexity, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: For complex $z_i$, the quantity $\sum_i w_i z_i$ can be complex and hence cannot be minimized using the usual order; it can also cancel and is not an $\ell^1$ norm. Thus both weighted optimization programs are ill-defined as written, and the weighted recovery theorem cannot apply to them.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\|z\|_{1,w}=\sum_i w_i|z_i|$ and require positive weights when it is called a norm; the intrinsic weights used in the corollary satisfy this positivity requirement.
issues.overall_effect: The weighted SR-LASSO estimator underlying the compressed-sensing guarantee, and the weighted QCBP variant, are not valid optimization problems as displayed.
issues.title: The weighted ell-one objective is not a norm and is not orderable over complex vectors
issues.why_classification: The standard absolute-value correction is local and preserves the intended decoders and all advertised guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exist a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathbb{C}^d$, with $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{K}$

Then the map $\bm{f}:\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d\to\C^{|V|}$ defined by $\bm{f}( \bm{y} )= \bm{u(}T, \bm{y} )$ satisfying problem \eqref{eq:ted} admits a holomorphic extension $\tilde{\bm{f}}$ to $\mathring{\mathcal{K}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix requires $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal K$, while the theorem additionally requires $\mathcal K\subset\mathcal U$. Hence $\mathcal K=\mathcal U$. Viewed as a subset of $\mathbb C^d$, the real cube $\mathcal U$ has empty complex interior, so holomorphy on $\mathring{\mathcal K}$ gives no extension to a complex neighborhood. More generally, the assumption alone also does not ensure that $\mathcal U$ lies in $\mathring{\mathcal K}$, which is required for a function on $\mathring{\mathcal K}$ to extend all of $f$.

failure_location.quote: satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:diffusion_matrix} for some compact $\mathcal{K}\subseteq\C^d$ such that $\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{U}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incompatible inclusion by the neighborhood condition $\mathcal U\subset\mathring{\mathcal K}$ (or an equivalent open-neighborhood hypothesis), and consistently formulate the extension on that interior.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem does not establish the claimed nonvacuous holomorphic extension under its literal hypotheses, and its stated form cannot be invoked by the polynomial-approximation corollaries.
issues.title: The holomorphy theorem imposes incompatible domain inclusions
issues.why_classification: A standard local strengthening of the domain condition makes the proof applicable, while the downstream corollaries already impose the stronger polyellipse inclusion and therefore retain their intended regimes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $ \bm{c} =(c_{\bm{\nu}})$ be the sequence of coefficients of $f_v$ with respect to either the Chebyshev or Legendre basis
$\varrho$ be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary never specifies $\varrho$ or links it to the selected polynomial basis. The Legendre and Chebyshev systems are orthonormal for different measures, and the sampling/recovery guarantee cannot hold for an arbitrary unspecified measure, for example one concentrated on too few points.

failure_location.quote: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ be the number of samples, drawing $\bm{y}_1, \dots, \bm{y}_m$ independently from the measure $\varrho$, and $0 < \epsilon < 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the uniform measure with the Legendre basis or the Chebyshev measure with the Chebyshev basis, consistently with the preceding approximation framework.
issues.overall_effect: The probability and recovery bounds in cor:CS are unsupported for the full class of sampling measures allowed by its statement.
issues.title: Compressed-sensing guarantee leaves the sampling measure unrestricted
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard basis-matched sampling hypothesis is local and preserves the compressed-sensing rates and intended experimental setting.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ that admits a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}} \subset \mathbb{C}^d$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed noiseless error bound is independent of the amplitude of $f$. If a holomorphic function not represented exactly by the finite space is replaced by $Af$, then its least-squares approximation error scales by $|A|$, whereas the displayed right-hand side is unchanged. The paper's own best-term estimate includes the necessary factor $\|f\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal E_\rho)}$. Corollary cor:LS likewise omits the available diffusion bound depending on $u_0$ and $M$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply the approximation term by an appropriate holomorphic-extension norm, and in cor:LS bound that norm by the quantity supplied by thm:mainthm. The algebraic rate may remain unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Neither the auxiliary theorem nor the graph-diffusion least-squares corollary provides a valid error estimate uniformly over the stated functions or initial data.
issues.title: Least-squares error bound is missing dependence on the size of the target function
issues.why_classification: The rate can be preserved, but the advertised amplitude-independent guarantee must be materially weakened by introducing problem-dependent norm or diffusion factors.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $0<\epsilon < 1$, $\varrho$ be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$, $m \geq 3$

issues.failure_explanation: The parameter $p$ occurs in the constant and convergence exponent of th:main_ls and cor:LS but is never introduced or quantified in either statement. Consequently, the asserted rate is not a well-formed mathematical conclusion, and different choices of $p$ give materially different exponents.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the admissible range of $p$ and whether the estimate holds for every fixed $p$ in that range, consistently with the invoked holomorphic approximation result.
issues.overall_effect: The precise algebraic rate claimed for least-squares surrogates is undefined as stated.
issues.title: The least-squares convergence statements contain an unquantified exponent parameter
issues.why_classification: Quantifying the already-used regularity parameter is a short local repair that does not otherwise alter the method or its rate family.
